chunks: My father (RA) narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Jamil ibn Durraj, from Abu Abdillah (AS)

He said: I asked him about the children of the Prophets (AS), and he replied: They are not like the children of other people. I asked him about Ibrahim, son of the Messenger of Allah (SA), if he had remained alive, would he have been a truthful one (Siddiq)? He said: If he had remained alive, he would have been upon the path of his father (SA).
ai.seo_question: What is the status of the children of the Prophets in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to illustrate the concept of *fitrah* (innate disposition) and the elevated spiritual status of the Prophet's offspring, distinguishing them from general humanity. By citing Ibrahim, the son of Muhammad (SAW), as a potential *Siddiq* (truthful one) had he lived, the Imam affirms their inherent alignment with divine truth and prophetic legacy. This supports the Shia view that the progeny of the Prophets possess a unique, innate guidance that distinguishes their spiritual trajectory from that of ordinary people.
